_about: The single source of truth for every mechanic term. codex is the rule as the player reads it; design.holes is what the mechanic does not do yet. docs/vocabulary.md is generated from this file by tools/export_vocabulary.gd. status: implemented (in sim/), planned (designed, not coded), idea (floated, undecided).

entries.name: Hull
entries.codex: Damage that gets past shield removes hull. Hull never recovers during a battle. At zero the mech is a wreck to be salvaged after the battle.

entries.name: Shield
entries.codex: Enemy damage hits shield before hull, and a standing shield blocks a blow whole: however small the shield and however big the blow, nothing bleeds through to the hull (a breaching foe is the exception). The blow still costs the shield its damage. Shield components add shield up to the chassis maximum; in a fight that is the only way shield comes back. Out of combat it returns each battlefield phase at the chassis's field rate. It never refills for free between skirmishes.

design.holes: Rates and shield sizes are placeholders. Decided 18 September: block-the-blow replaced bleed-through, and the in-combat trickle was dropped the same day (a passive may bring it back for one chassis).

entries.name: Heat
entries.codex: Attack components may add heat. At the end of the round, heat above the chassis maximum burns hull one for one and the gauge settles at the maximum; until then a vent can still bring it down. Vent components remove heat. At the start of every turn a mech sheds its chassis's cooling rating in heat, so a round spent on ballistics or shields is a way of cooling down without a vent; Overheating ticks at the end of the round, after the enemy has struck, so a scorch lands on the round's peak heat before cooling relieves it.

design.holes: Heat does nothing below the cap. Consider effects at high heat short of overflow. Cooling numbers are placeholders; cooling must stay below a typical weapon's heat or heat never matters, and a vent component must be worth a whole turn (tuning).

entries.name: Reroll
entries.codex: Three rerolls per round, each rerolling every unlocked, unspent mech die. A reroll always lands on a different component: never the one showing, never one equivalent to it (a die whose components are all alike keeps what it shows). Rerolls may be spent before or after attacking, so a low damage roll is information for the rest of the round. Never pooled across rounds.

entries.name: Rift Pressure
entries.codex: Ticks once per battlefield phase and once per skirmish round. When full it resets and a fresh pack emerges at the rift.

design.holes: Spawns a fixed pack. Should draw from the battle's faction(s) and escalate.

entries.name: Gate Integrity
entries.codex: A pack whose path reaches the gate strikes it instead of moving. Gate integrity persists across battles and is repaired in the meta.

design.holes: Gate damage formula is a placeholder (strength divided by three).

entries.name: Attack component
entries.codex: Spend on a foe within reach to deal its power in damage, then apply its keywords and heat.

entries.name: Shield component
entries.codex: Spend on self or an ally to add its power in shield, capped at that mech's shield maximum.

entries.name: Vent component
entries.codex: Spend on self or an ally to remove its power in heat.

entries.name: Buff component
entries.codex: Equipment spent on a machine (itself, an ally, or either, as the component says) that grants it a status, so many stacks deep, through the end of so many rounds: Overcharged for damage, Braced against damage, Primed to burn on hit. The die shows the status name and the stacks.

design.holes: Only one component carries it, a draft. Debuffs on foes stay weapons.

entries.name: Cracked component
entries.codex: A cracked component still acts but loses all keywords and unique effects. Cracked compoents can still crit, still generate heat, and still provide their passive bonuses and abilities. A destroyed component is blank and does nothing when it comes up, and provides passive bonuses but not passive abilities. Both persist until repaired in the hangar.

entries.name: Damage range
entries.codex: A kinetic attack component shows a minimum and a maximum and rolls between them when spent, immediately and visibly. Energy components show one number and never roll. Numbers are in tens.

design.holes: Ranges are content-authored per component; no upgrade path raises min or max yet.

entries.name: Critical hit
entries.codex: A kinetic component may carry a crit chance. On a crit the roll is multiplied by the crit multiplier: a base of 2 for everyone, plus every crit damage bonus that applies, from the component itself or a passive. Bonuses add to the multiplier, never multiply each other, so a +0.5 weapon with a +0.5 passive crits for 3 times. The readout shows the resulting multiplier. Energy components never crit. Crits fire the on_crit passive trigger.

design.holes: The base is Face.CRIT_MULT, a balance knob; lower it if crit triggers make crits too strong at low chance.

entries.name: Melee
entries.codex: Targets any front-rank foe. Can target any back-rank foe when the front rank is empty.

entries.name: Line of sight
entries.codex: Targets any front-rank foe, and any back-rank foe whose column is exposed.

entries.name: Indirect
entries.codex: Targets any foe in either rank. Hitting the front rank triggers danger close.

entries.name: Spread
entries.codex: Player keyword. Also hits the foes in the neighbouring columns of the target's rank.

entries.name: Penetrate
entries.codex: Player keyword. Hits first the front, then the back rank of a single column.

entries.name: Overwhelm
entries.codex: Player keyword. When a blow kills a front-rank foe, what it had past the kill carries into the foe behind it in the same column. Nothing stands behind a massive foe.

design.holes: Built 29 September. The spill is plain damage: it spends a shock and feeds a devour, and carries no other keyword of the blow. The Wild Boar's Juggernaut Drive grants it to every attack (grant_keyword, the first passive to add a keyword).

entries.name: Burn
entries.codex: Player keyword. Burning enemies lose 5 HP per stack at the start of their action, then lose one stack. Bypasses armour. Can be resisted.

entries.name: Corrode
entries.codex: Player keyword. Corroding enemies lose 1% of their HP per stack at the start of their action, then lose one stack. Bypasses armour. Can be resisted.

entries.name: Suppress
entries.codex: Player keyword. The target skips its telegraphed action this round, then gains two stacks of Numbed (three if massive). A foe may shrug it off: its own stun resistance plus 10% a Numbed stack.

entries.name: Numbed
entries.codex: Foe status. Each stack is 10% resistance to a suppress on top of the foe's own; a suppress it shrugs off does nothing and adds no stack. Loses a stack at the start of each of its turns, so a stun repeated on one foe stops landing while stuns spread across the formation keep working.

design.holes: Decaying since 26 September (was permanent for the fight); numbers are placeholders, to be judged against skirmish and boss-fight lengths.

entries.name: Stun resistance
entries.codex: A foe's base chance to shrug off a suppress, before Numbed. Rank and file have none; bosses carry some.

design.holes: 30 on the three bosses as a placeholder.

entries.name: Volatile
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any kind of component. Spending it bites its owner for 10 hull, past shield and armour, before the component acts. A blank is never spent, so a disabled entry does not bite.

design.holes: The Arsenal's self-damage (Ryan, 28 September), built 29 September: hull outright where the Corrupted bite takes shield first. The bite is a placeholder number (Skirmish.VOLATILE_BITE). It will feed the Nemesis's Crucible Capacitor once that counts blows that reach hull.

entries.name: Devour
entries.codex: Player keyword. Every foe this component kills gives its owner a stack of Overcharged for the skirmish; the stacks fade one a round at the round's end.

design.holes: The Ammit's talons (28 September), built 29 September on the kill in the attack resolution: a spread that kills two feeds two, a chain feeds on every link. The Quintessence Tap, which stops the fade and keeps the stacks for the battle, is planned.

entries.name: Weapon
entries.codex: A component spent on a foe within its reach. It need not deal damage.

entries.name: Equipment
entries.codex: A component spent on a machine: itself, an ally, or either, as the component says. Shields and vents are equipment.

design.holes: Buffs will be equipment too, once they exist.

entries.name: Targets
entries.codex: Whom a piece of equipment may be spent on: self and allies, self only, or allies only. Shown as a chip on the die when narrowed.

entries.name: Execute
entries.codex: +100% damage against a foe at or below half its health. Reduced to +50% against bosses and elites.

entries.name: Chain
entries.codex: If this attack kills an enemy, repeat it on a new, valid target.

entries.name: Rapid
entries.codex: After this component is spent, it is switched off for the rest of this round, the die rerolls for free (never the same entry), and the mech may act again. The switch-off only stops an infinite turn.

entries.name: Steady
entries.codex: A component with steady always uses its average damage as its base damage. It may still crit.

entries.name: Disable
entries.codex: Enemy keyword. The component the target's die is showing is switched off through the target's next turn: if the die lands on it, it comes up blank.

entries.name: Corrupt
entries.codex: Foe attack keyword. Each blow that lands leaves a stack of Corrupted on the component the target's die is showing: it deals damage to its owner whenever spent.

design.holes: No foe carries it yet; Ryan places it (The Chorus, presumably).

entries.name: Cleanse
entries.codex: Player keyword, on shield and vent components. Whoever the component is spent on also loses every Disabled, Corrupted and Overheating status. A rapid component's own switch-off is not a status a cleanse touches.

design.holes: No component carries it yet; Ryan places it.

entries.name: Energy Armour
entries.codex: Player status. Until end of round, attacks that strike shield are reduced by a flat amount. Stacks.

entries.name: Scramble
entries.codex: Player keyword. Randomize the enemy's intended target.

entries.name: Confuse
entries.codex: Player keyword. Randomize the enemy's intended target to target another enemy instead.

entries.name: Retaliate
entries.codex: Mech status. While it lasts, a foe that strikes this machine's bare hull is Shocked. From buff equipment it lasts the rounds the component says; the Armadillo's Faraday Hull carries it always.

design.holes: Was flat damage equal to the component's power. Thorns scales with enemy blows and so inverts horde against boss; a debuff does not (Ryan, 28 September). The Armadillo's passive carries it always on.

entries.name: Shocked
entries.codex: Foe status. The next blow this foe takes deals double damage, then the status clears. A Shocked foe that strikes bare hull again takes 10. Never stacks.

design.holes: The Armadillo's retaliation (Ryan, 28 September): the tank sets up kills instead of out-damaging area weapons against a horde, and it works on a boss. The discharge on a second strike is the small thorns left in. Numbers are placeholders.

entries.name: Overcharged
entries.codex: Mech status. Each stack is +10% damage on this machine's attacks. From buff equipment it lasts through the rounds the component says; from devour it lasts the skirmish and loses a stack at the end of each round unless a passive says otherwise.

design.holes: The buff side and devour run (29 September); a buff's stacks and devour's are the same status to the machine and add up. The Ammit's Quintessence Tap (which stops the decay and keeps the stacks for the battle, never the campaign) is planned. Name is a placeholder.

entries.name: Braced
entries.codex: Mech status. Takes 15% less damage per stack. Granted by buff equipment for the rounds it says.

design.holes: Placeholder name and number (29 September).

entries.name: Primed
entries.codex: Mech status. Every blow this machine lands leaves a stack of Burning per stack of Primed. Granted by buff equipment for the rounds it says.

design.holes: Placeholder name (29 September).

entries.name: Disabled
entries.codex: Component status. This die entry comes up blank while it lasts; the component itself is untouched. A foe's disable lasts through the mech's next turn and can be cleansed; a rapid component's own switch-off ends with the round.

entries.name: Corrupted
entries.codex: Component status. Every time this die entry is spent it bites its owner for 10 per stack, shield first, before the component acts. A blank is never spent, so a disabled entry does not bite. Stacks. Clears at end of skirmish. Can be cleansed.

design.holes: The bite is a placeholder number (Skirmish.CORRUPT_BITE_PER_STACK).

entries.name: Phased
entries.codex: Player and enemy status. This unit cannot attack, nor can it be damaged by attacks, until end of round.

entries.name: Taunt
entries.codex: Player keyword on shield and vent components, and the status it leaves. Until the end of the round every front-rank foe targets whoever the component was spent on; they turn at once, intents and all, and a foe that loses its target picks the taunting machine. A buff component may grant it too.

design.holes: Ryan, 28 September: an accessible keyword, not a locked one; the game needs more damage redirection or a tank has no reason to be in the fight. The family to build: taunt (front rank), beacon (back rank), a swap of targeting with an ally, an interpose that takes a blow aimed at an ally.

entries.name: Beacon
entries.codex: Player keyword on shield and vent components, and the status it leaves. Until the end of the round every back-rank foe targets whoever the component was spent on, the way a taunt draws the front. A massive foe stands in both ranks and follows either.

entries.name: Burning
entries.codex: Foe status. Loses 5 HP per stack at the start of its action, then loses one stack. Bypasses armour. Applied by the burn keyword, one stack per twenty damage dealt.

entries.name: Suppressed
entries.codex: Foe status. Skips its action this round, then clears.

entries.name: Cracked component
entries.codex: Mech status, global rule. When a blow lands on bare hull (no shield standing) and what gets past armour is at least a quarter of maximum hull, the mech's die is rolled and the component it lands on is injured. An intact component cracks: it loses its keywords and unique effects, but still does its basic action, can still crit, still generates heat, and still provides its passive bonuses and abilities. Any shield standing, however small, prevents injury, except against a breach; a foe's double strike is the other way past it. A cracked component stays cracked across skirmishes and battles until repaired in the hangar.

design.holes: Threshold is a placeholder. Repair cost and the hangar screen are not built.

entries.name: Destroyed component
entries.codex: Mech status. When an injury lands on a component that is already cracked, it is destroyed: blank, it does nothing when it comes up, and provides its passive bonuses but not passive abilities. until the hangar repairs or replaces it. An injury that lands on a destroyed component or an empty hardpoint finds nothing to break, so a badly broken mech shrugs off more of them.

entries.name: Front rank
entries.codex: Three slots. Front-preferring foes fill these. Always in line of fire.

entries.name: Back rank
entries.codex: Three slots behind the front. Back-preferring foes hold these.

entries.name: Exposed
entries.codex: A back-rank foe is exposed when the front slot in its column is empty. Exposed foes are in line of fire.

entries.name: Reinforcements
entries.codex: Foes not yet on the field. Front and Back ranks have their own reinforcement pool. Empty slots refill from the pool of reinforcements after each round. The skirmish is won when the field and all reinforcements are defeated.

design.holes: Elites should surface at set points rather than in pool order.

entries.name: Splash
entries.codex: Indirect fire on the front rank damages the firing unit equal to half the component's power, rounded up.

entries.name: Massive
entries.codex: A massive foe fills both slots of a column and counts as front rank. Its column is never exposed while it stands. Only some elites and bosses are massive.

design.holes: Cleave treats it as a front-rank neighbour; pierce cannot hit anything behind it because nothing is.

entries.name: Withdraw
entries.codex: Available at any point of the player's turn, the first round included. The price is always the same: the enemy takes its turn, then the team flees at the end of the round, so nobody leapfrogs out of contact unscathed. Ends the skirmish; survivors on both sides carry their damage to the battlefield. Shields do not refill on withdrawing; they recharge at the field rate only in phases spent out of combat.

entries.name: Movespeed
entries.codex: Movement points per phase. Entering a hex costs its terrain's move cost for that unit's traits.

entries.name: Intent
entries.codex: Each pack's path for the phase is previewed exactly. It heads for the gate or the nearest city defense, or hunts mechs if aggro. Player routes resolve first.

design.holes: Aggro is a fixed flag. Should be a behaviour per foe type.

entries.name: Body block
entries.codex: A pack stops at the first hex on its path occupied by a blocking unit. Flyers do not block; packs pass through their hex but never land on it.

entries.name: Contact
entries.codex: After all movement, every connected group of adjacent units that contains both sides becomes one skirmish. Multiple skirmishes resolve one at a time.

design.holes: No participant cap. May need one for phone readability.

entries.name: Pack
entries.codex: An enemy hex is a pack: one foe type times a strength. A skirmish's enemy composition is whatever packs are chained together at contact, so the rift's formation and the player's disruption of it decide what you fight. Bosses are single three-hex units.

entries.name: Footprint
entries.codex: A unit covers one or more hexes. A boss covers three in a triangle. Every footprint hex blocks, touches for contact, and is a tap target. Packs and mechs stay single-hex.

design.holes: Footprints do not rotate with facing.

entries.name: Structure
entries.codex: Gate and rift hexes are structures wider than one hex. Nobody stands on them. A pack whose path reaches any gate hex strikes the gate.

design.holes: The rift does nothing yet beyond marking where packs spawn.

entries.name: Spawn
entries.codex: When Rift Pressure fills, the next pack of the faction's spawn list appears on the nearest free hex to the rift.

design.holes: A full spawn list should arrive together as a formation; pressure currently sends one pack at a time.

entries.name: Plain
entries.codex: Cost 1.

entries.name: Road
entries.codex: Cost 1.

design.holes: Tanks should move faster on roads. Not coded.

entries.name: Rough
entries.codex: Cost 2. Cost 1 for quads and flyers.

entries.name: Ruins
entries.codex: Cost 2. Cost 1 for quads and flyers.

design.holes: Designed as cover for the pack inside a skirmish. Skirmish terrain conditions are not coded.

entries.name: Water
entries.codex: Impassable except for hover and flyer.

design.holes: Designed to dampen burn inside a skirmish. Not coded.

entries.name: Mountain
entries.codex: Impassable except for flyer.

entries.name: Flyer
entries.codex: Ignores terrain cost, crosses water and mountains, cannot body-block.

entries.name: Hover
entries.codex: Crosses water.

entries.name: Walker
entries.codex: Rough and ruins cost 1.

entries.name: Tank
entries.codex: No effect yet.

design.holes: Intended: faster on roads.

entries.name: Stealth
entries.codex: Controls no ground: packs do not stop beside it. Joins a fight only when an ally is in it, or when it stopped a pack in its path.

design.holes: The Dingo (Ryan, 28 September): a support car that waits in the wings while the heavies get into position, then joins their fight, and never fights alone unless run into. Pays again when hunter packs exist.

entries.name: City defense
entries.codex: A static player-side unit. Packs path toward it, and it joins any skirmish it is adjacent to.

design.holes: Defenses have no die. They cannot act inside a skirmish yet.

entries.name: On attack
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires after the damage roll on every attack. Effects: multiply or add damage or heat, or set a minimum damage. An effect may carry a when condition: component_cracked (only when the component being spent is cracked).

entries.name: On shield gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this mech gains shield from any source.

entries.name: On heat gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this mech gains heat.

entries.name: On round start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires after the roll, before rerolls: shield from heat, a flat shield, a vent.

design.holes: Built 30 September for the Thermal Recoupler; the heat it reads is the gauge after the turn's passive cooling.

entries.name: On skirmish start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once when the skirmish begins.

entries.name: On foe status
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when any foe gains a status (Burning today; the buffs and debuffs to come), whoever applied it, and never for Suppressed or Numbed themselves. Effects: chance_suppress (a chance the foe is also Suppressed, rising per point of shield the owner is missing).

design.holes: One machine's passive so far (the Baboon's Pocket Paradox).

entries.name: On crit
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when an attack component crits. Effects: multiply or add damage, add burn to the target, vent the attacker's heat.

entries.name: On hull damage
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this mech loses hull.

design.holes: Hook for the pinned berserker idea.

entries.name: Out of combat
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires at the end of a battlefield phase in which this mech had no skirmish.

entries.name: Command die
entries.codex: One die rolled alongside the mech dice each round. Its entries are rechargeable commander abilities and never deal damage. They come from the hangar, never from rewards. Die size is a research path.

design.holes: Open question: whether the command die exists at all, or one-shots only.

entries.name: One-shot
entries.codex: Consumable ability. Pouch of three. Picked up from skirmishes, expires when the battle ends. Starting stock restocks every battle.

entries.name: Reward pick
entries.codex: After a skirmish victory: a modifier on a component you carry, a one-shot, or a battle-wide boon. Weighted by the pack's faction.

entries.name: City ability
entries.codex: Battlefield-level ability owned and upgraded by the city: sprint, airlift, teleport, tractor beam, orbital strike. Cooldowns measured in phases.

design.holes: Consider range limits from the gate so the push north leaves support behind.

entries.name: Cooldown
entries.codex: City abilities only. Counted in battlefield phases. Never used inside a skirmish.

entries.name: Component
entries.codex: A piece of equipment on a mech, and one entry on its die. There is no generic equipment: every entry on a die is a component, or an empty hardpoint. Each round the die is rolled and the component that comes up is what the mech can do.

design.holes: Multi-slot components were considered and scrapped on 18 September as invisible complexity.

entries.name: Hardpoint
entries.codex: A free slot on the chassis. Any component fits any hardpoint. On the model a hardpoint is a socket where the component mounts.

entries.name: Fixed component
entries.codex: A component built into the chassis: always on the die, never removed, never sold, and it uses no hardpoint. The Badger's claw and its plating are fixed.

design.holes: Decided against unlocking fixed slots for money (18 September).

entries.name: Empty hardpoint
entries.codex: A hardpoint with nothing in it is an entry on the die that does nothing when it comes up. Nothing fills it for you.

entries.name: on_injury
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when an injury lands on a component. Effects: no_destroy (a cracked component holds instead of being destroyed).

entries.name: Armour
entries.codex: A chassis number taken off every blow that lands on bare hull, flat, never a percentage. A blow smaller than the armour does nothing. Shield is not armoured: a blow on shield costs the shield its full damage.

design.holes: Numbers are placeholders. Armour from components is content, not yet written.

entries.name: Strike order
entries.codex: Foes strike in the order they stand: front rank left to right, then the back rank. Each blow is resolved on its own against the shield standing at that moment, so which foe strikes first decides what a small shield blocks. At first contact the heaviest hitters deploy left.

entries.name: Breach
entries.codex: A breaching blow overflows: what the shield cannot absorb reaches the hull, and if that is a quarter of maximum hull it injures a component like any bare-hull blow. It breaks the fundamental promise that a standing shield stops the big hit, so it is a dangerous, uncommon attack modifier, and its counterplay is not the shield: redirect it or interrupt it.

design.holes: A property of a foe's attack action. No foe carries it yet; Ryan places it. Redirect and interrupt do not exist yet. Name is a placeholder (pierce is taken by the player keyword).

entries.name: Foe action
entries.codex: A foe has a base attack, the quick read of how hard it hits, and a list of attacks that scale it. Each round every foe on the field picks one by weight before the player acts, so what it will do and to whom is announced exactly. An attack's damage is the base times its factor, and the help text shows the resulting number.

design.holes: Only attacks run; defend, buff and debuff actions stay planned. Weighted RNG is the whole brain for now.

entries.name: Vents all
entries.codex: An attack that fires the machine's whole heat as it is spent: the heat gauge is empty after the shot, and every 10 heat fired adds the component's bonus to the blow before crits and passives. The shot's own heat cost still lands.

design.holes: Built 30 September for the Afterburner Cannon (vents_all and power_per_heat on the face). Only the first shot of a chain fires the heat.

entries.name: Strikes
entries.codex: An attack's blows per use. A weapon with three strikes lands three separate hits: each rolls its own damage, its own crit and its own effects, so a rapid-fire weapon procs often. Against a shield, every strike past the first reaches the hull; against armour, every small strike loses the armour, so many small hits are the wrong tool for a heavy target and the right one for a soft one. Foe attacks have strikes too.

design.holes: Heat is paid once per use, not per strike. Foes have no armour yet, so on the player side strikes only matter for procs until they do.

entries.name: Static
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Always on. Its effects change a mech's numbers or a component's properties while a condition holds, rather than firing on an event: add_stat and multiply_stat on hull, shield, heat, armour, move or recharge; add_damage_taken and multiply_damage_taken on every incoming blow; set_reach on a component (the Badger's cracked weapons become melee); suppress, which turns off another effect by id or tag.

design.holes: Every read asks the pipeline; nothing is written to a stat or a component, so an effect that is gone stops answering. A static reach rule cannot be conditioned on reach.

entries.name: Order of operations
entries.codex: Everything that changes a number goes through one pipeline, in one order. Sources: the chassis passive and each fitted component's passive (until refitted), skirmish rewards (until the battle ends), buffs and debuffs (until the skirmish ends, or until the end of a given round). First suppression, shortest-lived source to longest: a live effect that suppresses another by id or tag turns it off, and a suppressed effect suppresses nothing. Then the gate: an effect takes part only if it is live, its trigger fires now, its condition holds, and, for an ability, its component is not destroyed (a destroyed component keeps its stat bonuses and loses its abilities). Then adds, all sources summed; then multiplies, all sources multiplied; then floors and caps; then overrides, where the shortest-lived source wins and the latest granted breaks ties. In an attack, the crit multiplier and the fixed keyword rule (execute) come before the pipeline's adds and multiplies. Nothing is ever stored as a total: every read asks again, so an effect that is gone stops answering. Statuses stack: the same status granted again adds stacks instead of a second copy; an add is worth its value per stack and a multiply is applied once per stack; a status that ticks applies its per-stack tick at its owner's turn, then loses one stack, and is gone at zero.

design.holes: Refit (the hangar) is what changes loadout-scoped effects; not built.

entries.name: Overheating
entries.codex: Mech status. Gains 5 heat per stack at the end of the round, after the enemy has struck, then loses one stack. The mech-side counterpart of Burning: metal does not burn, it heats. Applied by foe attacks that scorch. Clears at end of skirmish. Can be cleansed.

design.holes: Placeholder name and numbers, engine id overheating; Ryan is looking for the flavour.

entries.name: Scorch
entries.codex: Foe attack keyword. Each blow that lands leaves one stack of Overheating on the mech it hit.

design.holes: Placeholder name. No foe carries it yet; Ryan places it (fire demons, presumably).
